gaps.sentence: The programme ___ I watched last night was about volcanoes.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things, even when it is the object of the clause.

gaps.sentence: Is this the street ___ the accident happened?
gaps.explanation: 'Where' introduces information about location; 'the street which the accident happened' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: I've told you everything ___ you need to know.
gaps.explanation: After 'everything', 'that' is used (and may be omitted); 'which' is avoided after 'everything'.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ hand in their essays late will lose marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to the students performing the action; the verb 'will lose' follows later in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: Do you remember the time ___ we got lost in Rome?
gaps.explanation: 'When' introduces defining clauses after 'the time'; 'which' would need a preposition.

gaps.sentence: My colleague Anna, ___ joined us in May, has already been promoted.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to Anna; non-defining clauses never use 'that'.

gaps.sentence: The bridge ___ the campaign saved has just been listed as a monument.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' relates to the bridge, the object of 'saved'.

gaps.sentence: This is the hotel ___ we stayed last summer.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' means 'in which' and needs no preposition; 'the hotel which we stayed' would be ungrammatical.
